[page[title]]

Console command applications must declare a root IHostExtensions composition class.

What the Standard says

“entry point” — The Standard describes configuration models as system entry points that route startup behavior. A root IHostExtensions class gives a command application one visible composition point for that responsibility. read it here.
“command lines” — The Standard explicitly recognizes command-line interfaces as exposure components. The root host extension is cCoder's concrete application of that exposure boundary. read it here.

Why it matters

A command-line app needs one root that translates host invocation into an application command. IHostExtensions provides that boundary without turning Program.cs into a command parser, dispatcher, and business service at once.

Bad code example

// Program.cs resolves and runs commands directly.

Good code example

public static class IHostExtensions
{
    public static ValueTask RunAsync(this IHost host, string[] args) =>
        host.RunCommandAsync(args);
}
